'''Mary Jean Garson''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|AM|FAA}} (born 6 November 1953) is a British-Australian organic chemist and academic. She is an Emerita Professor in the School of Chemistry and Molecular Biosciences at the [[University of Queensland]].

== Early life ==
Garson was born in [[Rugby, Warwickshire|Rugby]], England,<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|year=2010|title=Under the microscope: Professor Mary Garson (NC 1971)|journal=Newnham in Australia: Newsletter|volume=September 2010}}</ref> the daughter of an engineer and botanist.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/diversity/175-faces/all-faces/professor-mary-garson-cchem-frsc|title=Professor Mary Garson CChem FRSC {{!}} 175 Faces of Chemistry|website=www.rsc.org|language=en|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327101958/http://www.rsc.org/diversity/175-faces/all-faces/professor-mary-garson-cchem-frsc/|archivedate=27 March 2019}}</ref> She took her B.A with Honours from the [[University of Cambridge]], [[Newnham College, Cambridge|Newnham College]] in 1974. Garson's focus was the natural sciences, specializing in chemistry. She obtained an MA in Natural Sciences and she took her PhD in organic chemistry from Cambridge in 1977.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://staff.scmb.uq.edu.au/staff/mary-garson|title=Professor Mary Garson {{!}} School of Chemistry & Molecular Biosciences|website=staff.scmb.uq.edu.au|access-date=2017-06-09}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Garson won a [[Royal Society]] postdoctoral fellowship after her PhD, undertaking research in Rome, Italy from 1977 to 1978.<ref name=":0" /> She continued her research at [[Murray Edwards College, Cambridge|New Hall]] at Cambridge on a college research fellowship from 1978 to 1981.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.eoas.info/biogs/P004920b.htm|title=Garson, Mary – Biographical entry – Encyclopedia of Australian Science|last=Centre|first=The University of Melbourne eScholarship Research|website=www.eoas.info|language=en-gb|access-date=2017-03-23}}</ref> She worked as a medicinal chemist from 1981 to 1983 at [[Smith, Kline & French|Smith Kline and French]] Research Ltd in [[Welwyn]], England,.<ref name=":2" />

Garson won a Queen Elizabeth II Research Fellowship from [[James Cook University]] (1983–1986), based in the Townsville region to research the bioactive organic chemicals in marine organisms. In Townsville, she undertook dive training to study on the [[Great Barrier Reef]].<ref name=":0" /> Garson then took a teaching/research position as the first female academic in chemistry at the [[University of Wollongong]], before moving to the [[University of Queensland]] as a lecturer in 1990. She was promoted to Senior Lecturer in 1992 and Reader in 1998.<ref name=":2" /> She researches and publishes on the structure, biosynthesis and function of natural products, especially those from marine invertebrates and other microorganisms.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://smah.uow.edu.au/content/groups/public/@web/@sci/@chem/documents/doc/uow130422.pdf|title=Mary J. Garson|access-date=March 23, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Stewart|first=Doug|date=1 July 1999|title=Sponges get respect|journal=International Wildlife|volume=29|issue=4|pages=27|via=Factiva}}</ref> She also researches the chemistry of South East Asian medicinal plants.<ref name=":1" />

Garson was promoted to Professor in the School of Chemistry and Molecular Biosciences in 2006, and has served as Deputy Head of the School from 2005 to 2009. Since 2021, she is an Emeritus Professor of Chemistry at the university.{{cn|date=October 2024}}

== Awards and honours==
*2009 – Our Women, Our State (Queensland Government) – Highly Commended<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://statements.qld.gov.au/Statement/Id/67314|title=University team wins women's award|access-date=2017-03-23|language=en-AU}}</ref>
*2011 – Leighton Medal of the [[Royal Australian Chemical Institute]], in recognition of her contributions and leadership to the chemistry community, within Australia and overseas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raci.org.au/events-awards/2011|title=2011 Award Winners – The Royal Australian Chemical Institute Incorporated|website=www.raci.org.au|access-date=2017-03-23}}</ref>
*2013 – Distinguished Woman in Chemistry or Chemical Engineering award of the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry{{cn|date=October 2024}}
*2014 – named as one of "175 Faces of Chemistry" by the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], UK{{cn|date=October 2024}}
*2017 – inaugural Margaret Sheil Women in Chemistry Leadership award of the Royal Australian Chemical Institute{{cn|date=October 2024}}
*2018 - Royal Society of Chemistry, Australasian lecturer (by invitation){{cn|date=October 2024}}
*2019 – [[Member of the Order of Australia]] (AM) in the [[2019 Australia Day Honours|Australia Day Honours]] for "significant service to education, particularly to organic chemistry, and as an advocate for women in science".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/2003395|title=Professor Mary Jean Garson|website=honours.pmc.gov.au|access-date=2019-01-26}}</ref>
*2023 – named as a Distinguished Fellow of the Royal Australian Chemical Institute{{cn|date=October 2024}}
*2024 – elected Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy announces 2024 Fellows for outstanding contributions to science |url=https://www.science.org.au/news-and-events/news-and-media-releases/academy-announces-2024-fellows-for-outstanding-contributions-to-science |access-date=2024-05-22 |website=Australian Academy of Science |language=en}}</ref>

A species of marine flatworm, discovered at [[Heron Island Research Station|Heron Island]], is named for her ''Maritigrella marygarsonae''.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.businessweekly.co.uk/news/biomedtech/cambridge-innovators-inspire-future-nobels-curies-and-faradays|title=Cambridge innovators to inspire future Nobels, Curies and Faradays {{!}} Business Weekly {{!}} Technology News {{!}} Business news {{!}} Cambridge and the East of England|website=www.businessweekly.co.uk|language=en|access-date=2017-03-23}}</ref>

== Memberships ==
*President-Royal Australian Chemical Institute (Queensland Division)
*Chair, International Relations Committee of RACI
*Member, National Committee for Chemistry
*Executive Secretary, World Chemistry Congress/IUPAC General Assembly (2001)
*Chair, Board of Australian Science Innovations
*Organiser, Chemistry-Biotechnology Symposium at World Chemistry Congress (Torino, 2007); 27th International Symposium on the Chemistry of Natural Products (Brisbane, 2011)
*Organiser, Women sharing a Chemical Moment in Time, International Year of Chemistry (2011)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iupac.org/publications/ci/2011/3302/iw1_garson.html|title=Chemistry International – Newsmagazine for IUPAC|website=www.iupac.org|access-date=2017-03-23}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Women are good for chemistry|last=Garson|first=Mary|date=January 24, 2011|work=Courer Mail}}</ref>
*Leadership roles in Division III (organic and biomolecular) of International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) as Titular Member (2006-2007), Secretary (2008-2011), President-elect (2012–2013), Division President and Bureau Member (2014–2015), then as Past-President (2016-2017)<ref name=":1" />
*Elected to Membership of the Bureau of the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (2018-2021)
*Co-chair IUPAC100 (centennial) Management Committee (2016-2019)
*Co-convenor of Women's Global Breakfast networking event held in over 100 countries since 2019; the theme for the 2024 breakfast event on February 27 is "Catalyzing Change in Chemistry"
*Incoming Vice-President/President-elect, and Chair of the Science Board, of the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry for 2024-2025
